_doc: Corpus-completeness manifest (Arc 1 S4). One row per conformance-corpus
family: every test_fixtures/ subdirectory plus every workspace/tests/
entry. scripts/check_corpus_manifest.py enforces it in CI (the
workspace-json-fresh lane): required consumers present, active-port
symmetry where declared, no unknown families, no orphaned fixtures.
kind: source = hand-authored inputs; compiled = generated from a source
corpus or a canonical generator; fixtures = driver cases + pinned
goldens. required_consumers is the BLOCKING set (POLICY.md #1: active
ports rust+swift, the reference interpreter, and the scripts/ gates;
the frozen OCaml/Python-Qt ports run at the five-port-parity tag and
are deliberately untracked here). port_symmetry: the rust and swift
claimed sets (after the transitive data-reference closure) must be
identical for the family. claim_style is documentation of HOW each
consumer registers fixtures — the checker's extraction rules implement
TWO gap lists, of opposite shapes: known_gaps SUPPRESSES a named
mechanical check (and a row that suppresses nothing is reported stale);
coverage_gaps DECLARES what the corpus cannot reach at all and is
printed on every run. See _coverage_gaps_doc at the foot of this file.

test_fixtures/actions.notes: The ACTION-seam corpus (dispatch_action / dispatchYamlAction). Goldens (*_expected.json) and setup SVGs are claimed transitively via expected_json/setup_svg data references. Second branches of the toggle_all_layers_* actions (all-invisible->preview, all-outline->preview, all-locked->unlock) were reference-only pins (workspace/tests/phase3/) until S4 added the *_all_* port-side fixtures; the remaining phase3 panel-state-driven scenarios stay reference-only pending a port-side panel-seeding mechanism (a named future decision).

claim_style.rust: path literals (cross_language_test.rs + module-scattered tests, e.g. geometry/tspan.rs)
claim_style.swift: path literals (AlignFixtureTests full paths; TspanPrimitivesTests loadFixture)

test_fixtures/algorithms.notes: Port symmetry is deliberately NOT machine-checked per registration list here: every algorithm in cross_language_algorithms.py's ALGORITHMS dict is gated across both active ports by that script (each port's roundtrip binary runs every fixture), while the in-port unit registrations legitimately differ (Rust natively gates the pane/panel/menu vectors; Swift natively gates align + the tspan primitives). The count is not restated here on purpose -- it was stale at '14' while the dict held 15. The three PANEL vectors are in-port only (not in the ALGORITHMS dict, so not driven by the roundtrip binaries): panel_layout.json pins rects, panel_widget_tree.json pins structure, and panel_bind_values.json pins RESOLVED bind.* VALUES -- the last is also driven by the reference (test_bind_values.py), which additionally asserts the golden is not stale relative to it.

test_fixtures/artboards.notes: Reference-only BY DESIGN: the default-seeded artboard scenario drives interpreter panel/effect state that the ports cannot seed headlessly today; port-side panel-seeding is a named future decision. The ports gate artboard DOCUMENT semantics via the operations corpus (artboard_*.json) instead.

test_fixtures/character_apply.notes: CHARPANEL: the FIELD-SCOPED Character-panel apply law (transcripts/CHARACTER.md 'The field-scoped apply law'). Gates all THREE live implementations off one corpus: a panel edit names its field and only that field's attribute group is written, everything else preserved per element. Same defect class as the stroke_apply family, over sixteen attributes, plus a port divergence (Swift mitigated it in the panel VIEW, Rust not at all). The reference states the field -> group table (workspace_interpreter/character_law.py) and the ports mirror it. The reference arm additionally asserts the corpus REJECTS the whole-rebuild law it replaced, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. No scripts consumer: the law is a pure function pinned in-port, not an algorithm_roundtrip binary.

test_fixtures/concept_constraints.notes: conformance.json compiled from workspace/tests/concept_constraints.yaml; the check_*.sh freshness gate recompiles and byte-compares.

claim_style.rust: name-lists (json/binary/svg round-trip arrays) + assert_svg_parse helper calls + path literals
claim_style.swift: name-lists (jsonRoundtripAllExpected / binaryRoundtripAllExpected / binaryReadPythonFixtures) + assertSvgParse/assertWorkspaceFixture helper calls + path literals
claim_style.scripts: commutativity FIXTURE_NAMES + _golden() calls + structural-golden checkers (check_menu_structure.py, check_toolbar_structure.py)

test_fixtures/expected.notes: Rust-authored canonical goldens (parse/roundtrip expectations, .bin byte pins, dependency-index and workspace-layout goldens, structural goldens). Port symmetry is hand-maintained per name-list (the S5-symmetrized json/binary/svg arrays) rather than machine-checked: a per-file symmetry rule would false-red the legitimately single-consumer members (menu_structure.json and toolbar_structure.json are scripts-only structural goldens; dup_id_import.json and dup_id_compound_operand.json are parse-only). Orphan detection here is REAL (no glob claims this directory).

test_fixtures/expressions.notes: conformance.json compiled from workspace/tests/expressions.yaml. The reference gates the SOURCE yaml directly (test_expr.py), not this compiled artifact — so 'reference' is intentionally not required here but IS required on the workspace/tests/expressions.yaml row.

test_fixtures/gestures.notes: The canvas-tool-seam corpus (press/move/release through YamlTool). Goldens and setup SVGs claimed transitively.

test_fixtures/keys.notes: The key->action resolution corpus; goldens claimed transitively via expected_json.

claim_style.rust: path literals (run_operation_fixture calls + txn/drag_coalesce/recorded literals) + data references
claim_style.swift: runOperationFixture helper calls + path literals + data references

test_fixtures/operations.notes: The op_apply corpus — the journal/undo spine's byte gate. 60+ of these files exist ONLY as data references (expected_json / expected_journal_json inside the driver fixtures); the transitive pass claims them. Port symmetry here is the gate's founding case: the Swift registration set lacked tspan_ops.json until S4 forced the remediation.

claim_style.rust: path literal (read_fixture in src/cross_language_test.rs preservation_invariants) + data references
claim_style.swift: path literal (readFixture in CrossLanguageTests.swift preservationInvariants) + data references

test_fixtures/preservation.notes: The PRESERVATION corpus (transcripts/EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md §4.1, the DOCUMENT-LEVEL INVARIANT GATE). Unlike every other fixtures family here it pins no golden document: it asserts six invariants (id_uniqueness / id_survival / consumed_ids_die / fresh_ids / bystanders_unchanged / subject_fields_only) over the canonical test JSON before and after an edit. That is what lets ONE vector be evaluated identically by both ports while each fails on its OWN sites — a golden could not, since the ports diverge on exactly the keys the law legislates. Setup SVGs are claimed transitively via setup_svg. A vector may PIN a known violation per port (expected_violations); a pinned invariant is asserted to FAIL, so fixing the site turns the gate red until the pin is removed — a pin cannot rot into a silent suppression. scripts/check_preservation_corpus.py gates the DATA shape with five anti-vacuity guards (V1-V5).

test_fixtures/production_capture.notes: The production run_effects capture pins (OP_LOG.md section 9, 3b-B). Journal/document/re-derivation goldens are claimed transitively via the root-relative expected_*_json fields.

test_fixtures/stroke_apply.notes: STROKEWIDTH: the FIELD-SCOPED Stroke-panel apply law (transcripts/STROKE.md 'The field-scoped apply law'). Gates all THREE live implementations off one corpus: a panel edit names its field and only that field's attribute group is written, everything else preserved per element; plus the colour-only recolour route. The reference states the field -> group table (workspace_interpreter/stroke_law.py) and the ports mirror it. The reference arm additionally asserts the corpus REJECTS the whole-rebuild law it replaced, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. No scripts consumer: the law is a pure function pinned in-port, not an algorithm_roundtrip binary.

claim_style.rust: DIRECTORY GLOB (tests/cross_language_test.rs json_roundtrip_all_fixtures reads every svg/*.svg) + name-lists + data references

test_fixtures/svg.notes: Hand-authored SVG inputs. Rust's roundtrip test GLOBS the whole directory, so this family's orphan detection is VACUOUS by construction: any stray .svg is auto-exercised by the glob and can never be flagged orphaned here. Deletions must rely on the sibling expected/ family's REAL orphan signal (that is exactly how named_elements.svg was caught: its expected/named_elements.json partner was orphaned) plus review. Port symmetry not machine-checked: Swift's parse/roundtrip name lists are hand-symmetrized with Rust's (S5), while setup SVGs are shared via data references.

test_fixtures/workspace_operations.notes: The layout-op corpus (panel/pane vocabulary). Per-case goldens claimed transitively via expected_json; layout setups live in expected/ (the setup field) and are claimed transitively there.

workspace/tests/concept_constraints.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; its compiled conformance.json is the artifact the ports and the reference gate.

workspace/tests/concept_fitters.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

workspace/tests/concept_operations.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

workspace/tests/concepts.yaml.notes: Human-authored source; compiled artifact gated downstream.

claim_style.reference: os.path.join segments (test_expr.py runs the yaml directly)

workspace/tests/expressions.yaml.notes: The expression-language corpus source. The reference interpreter is the executable spec and runs the yaml directly; the ports run the compiled test_fixtures/expressions/conformance.json.

workspace/tests/gradient_primitives.yaml.notes: The gradient_tile / gradient_slider widget-primitive exercise fixture. Until S4 its only consumer was the NON-GATING flask reference renderer (jas_flask/tests/test_renderer.py) — i.e. no blocking consumer at all; test_gradient_primitives.py now structurally validates every gradient/stop and evaluates what the reference evaluator covers. Widget RENDERING of gradient_tile/gradient_slider remains unvalidated by any blocking consumer (the reference interpreter has no renderer) — an honest, known limit.

workspace/tests/phase3.notes: Reference-only layer-action scenarios. The glob is a DIRECTORY-level claim: orphan detection inside it is VACUOUS (any stray yaml is silently exercised, none can be flagged), and the consumer itself silently passes when the directory is missing — the corpus gate independently asserts the directory exists and is non-empty. Coverage honesty: the toggle_all_layers_* second branches pinned here were reference-only until S4 added port-side actions fixtures (toggle_all_layers_*_all_*.json); the panel-state-driven scenarios (delete_layer_selection_two_layers, duplicate_layer_selection_one_layer, new_layer_with_selection) REMAIN reference-only pending a port-side panel-seeding mechanism — a named future decision.

workspace/tests/set_effect.notes: Reference-only BY DESIGN: the set-effect matrix pins the interpreter's `set:` semantics (typing, nullability, shadowing, panel routing) at the spec level; the ports exercise set: through the panel/action corpora rather than this matrix. Glob claim — orphan detection vacuous, directory-existence asserted by the gate.

_coverage_gaps_doc: The SECOND gap list, and the opposite shape from known_gaps above.
known_gaps is a suppressor: each row names one mechanical check on one
family/file and downgrades its failure to a warning, so it can only
ever speak about a check this gate already runs. coverage_gaps records
what the gate does NOT check -- a family whose fixtures never reach the
interesting branch, a field no fixture sets, a divergence no
port-vs-port comparison can see. It suppresses nothing; every row is
printed on every run, precisely so a green gate stops implying a
completeness it never had.
Required keys: id, title, evidence, blocks, unblock (census optional).
`evidence` must be a claim someone can re-run, because a gap you cannot
state precisely is not ready to record. Every row below was re-measured
on this commit rather than copied from the census -- three census
figures did not survive that (noted in the rows), and the census's
hit_test/marquee row is not here at all because it has since CLOSED:
element_intersects_rect and element_intersects_polygon are now driven
by both roundtrip binaries over 6 of hit_test.json's 40 vectors.
Census rows 5.3, 5.6, 5.10 and 5.11 are deliberately absent: they are
real, but this pass did not re-verify them, and an unverified row here
would be the same false assurance the empty list was.

coverage_gaps.title: The preservation gate can only reach violations expressible in op_apply's verb vocabulary, so six of EDIT_SEMANTICS_FREEZE.md §3.5's rows stay invisible to it
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit by grepping the dispatchers. op_apply has exactly ONE boolean verb in each port (jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs `"boolean_union"`, JasSwift/Sources/Document/OpApply.swift `case "boolean_union"`) and ZERO verbs matching apply_mask / set_width_points / make_compound_shape / boolean_subtract / boolean_intersect / boolean_divide. No verb can produce a PARTIAL (control-point) selection either: the string `Partial` occurs once in the whole of op_apply.rs, inside a `#[derive(...)]`. Consequently these §3.5 rows are unreachable from this corpus: Swift `withMask` .path arm; Swift `withWidthPoints` .path arm; Rust `move_control_points` Rect->Polygon arm (needs a corner drag, i.e. a partial selection); Rust `make_compound_shape_with_op` duplicate id; the boolean SURVIVOR arms (subtract_front / subtract_back / crop / trim / divide) and their Swift `locked: false` + dropped name/id/toolOrigin/mask; and both blob-brush `fillRule` arms (a gesture, not an op). RE-MEASURED 2026-07-27, after the DIVIDE and MERGE arms were repaired in Rust: still exactly ONE boolean verb per port (grep -c for boolean_divide / boolean_merge / boolean_trim over jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs and JasSwift/Sources/Document/OpApply.swift returns 0 in BOTH files), so neither repaired arm is expressible as a shared vector. JasSwift's applyDestructiveBoolean does implement `case "divide"` and `case "trim", "merge"`, so the missing piece is the op-verb registration, not the arm.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Of the §3.5 table, this gate today catches the Rust UNION frontmost-id carry, the Swift withChildren class (5 vectors), and one of the 41 Swift inline Layer(/Group( literals. The rest of the table is not gated by anything cross-language. Named consequence as of 2026-07-27: the Rust DIVIDE arm (which handed every output region the designated operand's whole `common`, leaving two live elements wearing one id) and the Rust MERGE arm (which elected the frontmost contributor's whole `common` by z-order) were both repaired with per-port batteries in jas_dioxus/src/document/controller.rs's `preservation_law_tests`, and NEITHER repair is visible to any cross-language gate. The Swift twins of both arms are unaudited by this corpus for the same reason.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two independent routes, both fixture-plus-verb: (a) widen the op vocabulary with the missing boolean verbs and a mask/width-points setter, then add preservation vectors for the 1->1 survivor arms — where subject_fields_only is exactly the right predicate; (b) give the GESTURE corpus the same invariant gate, which reaches the blob-brush arms and the Rect corner drag that the op corpus cannot address. Route (a) is now the cheap one for these two arms specifically: registering `boolean_divide` and `boolean_merge` in both ports' op_apply dispatchers is additive (each delegates to an applyDestructiveBoolean arm that already exists in both), after which a divide vector over preservation_nested_attrs.svg pins id_uniqueness and fresh_ids directly. Expect the swift lane to need pins on that vector until JasSwift's boolean rebuild is brought to the same rule.

coverage_gaps.title: The six preservation invariants say nothing about the FIELDS of a freshly minted element, so the boolean result's lossy kind demotion and its dropped non-paint fields are invisible
coverage_gaps.evidence: The invariants are id_uniqueness / id_survival / consumed_ids_die / fresh_ids / bystanders_unchanged / subject_fields_only. Every one of them is keyed on an id that existed BEFORE the edit; a minted element has no before-image to diff against, so nothing in the set constrains it. Concretely, on the boolean_union_merges_two_rects vector both ports emit a single-ring `Polygon` — the §3.5 row 'Boolean flatten, single-ring arm, both ports' calls that a lossy demotion (a Polygon has no slot for widthPoints / strokeBrush / strokeBrushOverrides / fillRule) — and the gate reports nothing, because the invariants never look at the output's kind or its non-identity fields.
coverage_gaps.blocks: §3.3's unanimity carry, §3.6's per-op paint column, and T1's representation term (no lossy demotion) are all statements ABOUT the minted element. None of them is gated here.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Add a seventh declarative invariant to the vector shape — an `expected_output` block naming the required kind and the fields the result must carry (unanimous values, RESULT_FILL_RULE) — and implement it in both port gates. This is additive to the existing five vectors and needs no new op verbs.

coverage_gaps.title: Swift indexes text by grapheme cluster; Rust and the reference index by Unicode scalar, so no non-ASCII vector can be added to the three text families
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured through the roundtrip harnesses at char_width 10 on this commit. content "ae\u0301b" (4 scalars / 3 clusters): reference and Rust give char_count 4 with 4 glyphs, Swift gives 3 with 3. The ZWJ family emoji U+1F468 U+200D U+1F469 U+200D U+1F467 (5 scalars / 1 cluster): reference and Rust give 5, Swift gives 1. Total line advance now AGREES (40 and 50 both ports) because the injected measurer counts scalars; it is the per-glyph subdivision and every index derived from it that diverge. Root cause is `Array(content)` in TextLayout.swift and PathTextLayout.swift. (TextLayoutParagraph.swift was cited here in error: it contains ZERO `Array(` occurrences - it holds only the hyphenation/segment/counter helpers.)
coverage_gaps.blocks: text_layout, text_layout_paragraph and path_text_layout are ASCII-only families. The rust-vs-swift comparison has no oracle-holdout mechanism (only property_planar and exact_boolean get one), so a non-ASCII vector cannot be added and marked -- it would simply red the gate.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Move Swift's three layout files onto scalar indices, in the SAME sweep as TextEditSession/TypeTool/TypeOnPathTool, which do their cursor arithmetic in `Character` counts (`text.count`, `key.count == 1`) and would otherwise desync from the layout for exactly these strings.
coverage_gaps.census: 5.9(a), extended: the census called this a harness bug only. The harness half is fixed (HARNESSUNIT); this is the product half it was hiding.

coverage_gaps.title: element_bounds gates a function that ignores transform entirely -- now PINNED as such; the transform-aware bbox is gated by its own family, but still only for a single-layer path
coverage_gaps.evidence: Element::bounds / Element.bounds IGNORE common.transform in both ports -- measured through the two roundtrip binaries, a 10x10 rect at the origin carrying translate(100,50) reports [0,0,10,10] from Rust and from Swift alike. Every vector of element_bounds.json used to carry "transform": null, so that contract was UNPINNED: a port that started folding the matrix moved no golden. As of 2026-07-27 the family is 22 vectors, the last five carrying a live matrix and expecting the UNTRANSFORMED box (rect translate, ellipse rotate 45, cubic under a general matrix, a stroked line under scale(3) where the stroke still inflates and the matrix still does not, and a group under translate). Discrimination measured: teaching Rust's Element::bounds to corner-map the matrix reds exactly those five on both legs (oracle-vs-golden and rust-vs-swift) and leaves all 17 older vectors green; reverted. The transform-aware function is element_evaluated_bbox / elementEvaluatedBBox, driven by the element_evaluated_bounds family, now 17 vectors: the original 9 (all RECTS -- translate, non-uniform scale, rotate 45, skewX, a full composed matrix, an ancestor-only layer transform, an element-then-layer composition-order vector, a stroked geometric-vs-preview vector, and a no-transform control) plus 8 NON-RECT ones added the same day (rotated ellipse, cubic under the composed matrix, arc under a layer rotation, scaled group, each with a null-transform control). The non-rect vectors are what make the family's central choice observable: it maps the four CORNERS of the geometric bbox, which on a rect is indistinguishable from bounding the transformed shape and on an ellipse or curve is not (rotate 45 on a 60x40 ellipse: corner-mapped 70.7107 square vs a true 50.9902 square). Reference, Rust and Swift all corner-map, so that is the ratified rule, not a shared slip.
coverage_gaps.blocks: One narrower thing than before. Every vector of the evaluated family is still placed as layers[0].children[0], so the ancestor walk is exercised at ONE level -- a nested group chain, and a group whose CHILDREN carry transforms (geometric_children_bounds does not fold those), are still ungated. Whether Element::bounds SHOULD stay transform-blind remains an open product question rather than a corpus one; both ports agree, and the corpus now genuinely pins that agreement instead of merely reporting it.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Extend element_evaluated_bounds with group-nesting vectors once the runners can express a nested document (both build a fixed layer/child pair today). Separately, a ruling on whether the untransformed bbox is the intended contract of Element::bounds -- the five is_ignored vectors record the behaviour, they do not settle the question.

coverage_gaps.title: The flatten family gates flatten_path_commands; the flattener the boolean pipeline calls is in neither roundtrip binary
coverage_gaps.evidence: Both harnesses call flatten_path_commands / flattenPathCommands (jas_dioxus/src/bin/algorithm_roundtrip.rs and JasSwift/ToolsAlgorithm/AlgorithmRoundtrip.swift). flatten_path_to_rings / flattenPathToRings have 6 references each across the two ports' sources and zero in either harness.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A family-name audit reports flatten as covered while the subdivision the boolean pipeline depends on is uncovered.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Either drive flatten_path_to_rings from a family of its own, or state in the manifest row that flatten covers the command-level flattener only.

coverage_gaps.title: flatten.json has no arc command, so the A-degrades-to-a-line branch of the flattener is ungated
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-counted mechanically over the parsed fixture on this commit: 18 vectors, with 8 of them carrying a C and 4 a Q (8 C commands and 4 Q commands in total), and ZERO A commands. The census row this replaces said 3 vectors and no curve command at all -- true when it was written, and closed since by the cubic/quadratic vectors; the arc leg is what survives of it.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Both flatteners send SmoothCurveTo / SmoothQuadTo / ArcTo to their endpoint as a straight line, in a catch-all arm no vector enters. The same arm also carries the current-point write for those commands, which is the defect class cubic_then_quad_current_point_chain was added to catch for cubics.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture-only: add an arc vector, and one where an arc is followed by a command that reads the current point.

coverage_gaps.title: No fit_curve vector reaches the iterative refinement or the recursive split, so Schneider's algorithm is gated only through its first pass
coverage_gaps.evidence: Instrumented fit_cubic with per-branch probes and ran the fixture through the Rust harness on this commit: generate_bezier reached 3 times (the 3 vectors with n_pts > 2 -- collinear_points_one_segment, horizontal_line, vertical_line), and reparameterize, newton_raphson and the recursive split reached ZERO times, because every one of those fits within tolerance on the first pass. The other 4 of 7 vectors return at the points.len() < 2 guard or the n_pts == 2 early exit. NOTE: the census claimed none of the 7 reaches generate_bezier; that is over-wide -- 3 do.
coverage_gaps.blocks: reparameterize, newton_raphson and the recursive split carry the algorithm's actual difficulty and are unexercised by the corpus.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture-only: add a vector whose curvature exceeds the error tolerance on one segment, so the split fires.

coverage_gaps.title: The codec gates cover only the field subset some fixture happens to populate, and the most divergence-prone fields are populated by none
coverage_gaps.evidence: Across all 39 test_fixtures/expected/*.json (the census said 25 -- re-counted on this commit), the keys mode, mask, fill_gradient, stroke_gradient, fill_rule, tool_origin, dash_align_anchors and width_points appear in ZERO files.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A canonical-JSON before/after comparison catches a dropped field perfectly, but only for fields a fixture sets. The gate passes loudly and says nothing about the region where the known CommonProps/Document field losses live.
coverage_gaps.unblock: One maximal fixture per element type with every optional field set to a non-default value -- the single highest-leverage addition in the serialization domain.

coverage_gaps.title: The codec now round-trips control characters, but only two per-port unit tests say so -- the SVG-driven golden lane still carries none, and nobody has established whether an SVG fixture could express one
coverage_gaps.evidence: Replaces `codec-no-control-chars`, which is CLOSED: json_escape_string / jsonEscapeString escape U+0000-U+001F, test_fixtures/algorithms/canonical_json_string.json pins 23 vectors byte-for-byte in both ports, and multi_line_text_round_trips_through_test_json / multiLineTextRoundTripsThroughTestJson drive a newline-bearing Text through the document writer, the parser and the writer again in each port. What remains: all 39 test_fixtures/expected/*.json goldens are produced by parsing test_fixtures/svg/*.svg, and a scan of every file under test_fixtures/ and workspace/ on this commit (543 files) finds zero C0 bytes in any .json and zero U+007F anywhere, so no SVG-driven golden exercises the new escaping. Whether the two SVG parsers preserve a newline inside a <text> element was NOT measured.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The escaping rule is gated at the writer and at the document round trip, but the path an actual multi-line text element would travel in production -- SVG import, then serialise -- has no vector. A port whose SVG text parser collapsed or dropped a newline would pass every gate that exists today.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Measure first, then decide: probe both SVG text parsers for what they do with a literal newline in element content (XML whitespace handling is a real ruling, not an obvious one). If the two ports agree and preserve it, add one svg/ + expected/ pair with multi-line content. If they disagree, that divergence outranks the fixture and belongs with the Captain.

coverage_gaps.title: NARROWED (VIEWSEED, 2026-07-27): the runners can now express a non-identity view, and 9 vectors do, but 63 of the 72 action/gesture driver cases still run at the identity view
coverage_gaps.evidence: Re-measured on this commit. The grep this row used to cite -- zoom_level / view_offset across test_fixtures/ and workspace/tests/ -- now returns two files, test_fixtures/actions/view_state.json and test_fixtures/gestures/draw_rect_zoomed.json, where it returned none. Counting driver cases (a JSON array of objects carrying a `name`) across test_fixtures/actions/ and test_fixtures/gestures/: 72 total, 9 carrying a `view` block -- the 7 view-state action vectors, the zoomed Rect gesture, and none elsewhere. Both runners in both ports accept the seed (`seed_case_view` / `seedCaseView`), so a case that wants a non-identity view now only has to ask.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The zoom division is now gated for exactly ONE tool (Rect, through pointer_event_payload, which is shared by every YAML tool) and for the doc.zoom.* effect family. Everything downstream of a tool handler that re-reads the view for itself -- overlay hit radii, the handle/curve hit tests, the eraser and blob radii, anything comparing a SCREEN-space threshold against a DOCUMENT-space distance -- is still only ever exercised where zoom is 1.0. Mutation-measured: dropping the zoom division in pointer_event_payload reds exactly 2 of the 2668 Rust lib tests (the new gesture vector and the pre-existing recorder::fidelity lockstep_rect_draw_under_pan_zoom_is_faithful).
coverage_gaps.unblock: Per-family, and now cheap: add a `view` block to an existing case in each family whose tool reads a screen-space threshold. Highest value first -- a selection click/marquee at zoom != 1 (the hit radius), a path-eraser stroke (the historical bug), a paintbrush stroke (ditto). No machinery is needed for any of them.

coverage_gaps.title: LIVE DIVERGENCE, unpinnable here: zoom_in / zoom_out with no anchor params anchor at the viewport centre in Rust and at the canvas top-left corner in Swift
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit with a probe vector run through both action corpora, then deleted (it cannot land: pinning the spec value reds the swift lane, and pinning Swift's value would be a test whose expected value coincides with the bug). Seed view {zoom 2.0, offset (-100, -50), viewport 800x600}, action zoom_in with params {}. transcripts/ZOOM_TOOL.md 'Keyboard shortcuts and actions' (the table row reads 'Viewport center') and workspace/actions.yaml:302 both say the default anchor is the viewport centre, which gives (2.4, -200, -120) by that file's 'Anchor and clamp math' block. RUST PRODUCES EXACTLY THAT. Swift produces (2.4, -120, -60) -- the triple you get by anchoring at screen (0, 0). coverage_gaps.title: RESOLVED for the two known instances: art_along_path's and calligraphic_outline's first-subpath walkers both dropped the whole path on a leading ClosePath, in BOTH ports, and both are now fixed and gated by new conformance families. What remains OPEN is the CLASS -- there is no mechanical gate that a future first-subpath walker honours S-4
coverage_gaps.evidence: THE TWO INSTANCES, both measured red before the fix and green after, on this commit. (1) `flatten` (jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/art_along_path.rs) and `flattenArtPath` (JasSwift/Sources/Algorithms/ArtAlongPath.swift) both returned [] for d = [Z, M(3,2), L(13,2)] and [(3,2),(13,2)] without the leading Z; shared by art-along-path, pattern-along-path and the bristle brush. (2) NEWLY FOUND while enumerating the class for (1): `sample_stroke_path` (jas_dioxus/src/algorithms/calligraphic_outline.rs) and `sampleStrokePath` (JasSwift/Sources/Algorithms/CalligraphicOutline.swift) carried the identical bail-out, and Calligraphic is the Phase-1 DEFAULT brush -- a path whose `d` begins with Z stroked NOTHING. In both cases the close arm was `if cx != sx || cy != sy { emit }` followed by an unconditional return, and at a leading close cx == sx == cy == sy == 0. The two ports AGREED in both cases, which is exactly the class a port-vs-port comparison is blind to. WHAT NOW WATCHES THEM: two new cross-language families, `art_flatten` (test_fixtures/algorithms/art_flatten.json, 9 vectors) and `calligraphic_outline` (test_fixtures/algorithms/calligraphic_outline.json, 9 vectors), both registered in cross_language_algorithms.py's ALGORITHMS dict and driven by a new verb in each port's roundtrip binary; plus in-port batteries in all four files. The calligraphic goldens were derived by running the STRIPPED path (no leading Z) through the pre-fix binary -- a shape that code already computed correctly -- so no expected value is the bug's own output. THE CLASS ENUMERATION, with its method and its blind spot stated. Method: grep every `PathCommand::ClosePath =>` arm in jas_dioxus/src and every `case .closePath` in JasSwift/Sources, then read each one for the pattern 'walks a first subpath, keeps an (sx, sy) subpath start, and RETURNS or EMITS from the close arm'. Result: exactly two such functions per port, both now fixed. The arms that are NOT in the class, and why: `flatten_path_commands` and `flatten_path_to_rings` already honour S-4 (`!pts.is_empty()`, and a flush of an empty ring drops it); `arrow_trim`'s `dist(cur, sub_start) > EPS` is already a no-op at a leading close and does not return; `Controller`'s simplify walk flushes a buffer of fewer than two points harmlessly; the bounds walk sets `cx = sx` only; and the painter / renderer / codec / PDF arms forward the command rather than interpreting a subpath. BLIND SPOT: that is a grep plus a reading, the same kind of evidence that let this defect through the freeze's own audit list. A fifth walker added tomorrow is caught by nothing.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Nothing artist-visible is broken at these two functions any more. What is blocked is CLASS closure: S-4 is a ruling about a shape of code ('a ClosePath before any point has been established contributes nothing'), and the tree now honours it in four flatteners by four separate hand-written guards, of two different forms -- `out.is_empty()` where the accumulator holds vertices, and a `has_current` / `hasCurrent` flag where it holds samples a bare MoveTo does not emit. Nothing forces the fifth walker to choose either. The two ports could also drift apart at the NEW guards without a golden moving except through the two new families, which cover only the inputs their vectors name.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two candidates, neither taken here because both are design decisions rather than fixes. (a) Collapse the four walkers onto ONE shared subpath iterator that applies S-4 once, parameterised by per-caller step counts and accumulator -- the four differ in sampling policy, not in subpath grammar, so this is plausible but it is a refactor across two ports and would move goldens. (b) Add a corpus family that feeds EVERY registered path-consuming algorithm the same leading-Z probe and asserts each one's output equals its output on the stripped path -- a relational gate rather than a value gate, which the current runner cannot express (it compares against pinned `expected` lists). (b) is the cheaper of the two and is the one that would actually close the class.

coverage_gaps.title: Every codec gate compares canonical test-JSON strings, and the fields the BINARY codec drops are a strict SUBSET of the fields that oracle drops -- so no fixture can red-light a binary drop
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit by round-tripping ONE attribute-saturated Path through all three codecs in both ports (test_fixtures/expected/codec_field_survival.json is the resulting matrix; the gates are `codec_field_survival` in jas_dioxus/src/cross_language_test.rs and `codecFieldSurvival` in JasSwift/Tests/CrossLanguageTests.swift). The canonical test-JSON drops 12 of the 13 watched fields (everything but fill_rule). The binary codec drops 7: common.mode, common.mask, common.tool_origin, fill_gradient, stroke_gradient, stroke_brush, stroke_brush_overrides. That 7 is a strict SUBSET of the 12. Since assert_svg_parse, assert_svg_roundtrip, json_roundtrip_all_expected and binary_roundtrip_all_expected all compare `document_to_test_json` STRINGS, a fixture that set any of those 7 would be normalized back to default on the way IN and the gate would pass, green and vacuous. Two figures in census row #18 did not survive this measurement and are corrected here: the binary codec PRESERVES stroke.dash_align_anchors and width_points (pack_stroke carries the whole Stroke -- align, dash pattern, dash length, miter limit and both arrowheads; pack_width_points carries the profile for Line and Path). CORRECTION to this wave's own commit 35f8c251, which said the two ports' <path> elements share 'seventeen attributes in the same order': re-measured at HEAD by diffing both writers' output for one attribute-rich path, the elements are byte-identical and carry TWENTY-TWO attributes. The byte-identity held; only the count was wrong.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The census's own §5.4 prescription -- 'one maximal fixture per element type with every optional field non-default' -- is NOT EXECUTABLE against the string oracle, so the repair it names cannot be scheduled as written. Concretely, a one-port slot in `pack_common` or `pack_element` lands silently: today the two ports agree cell for cell, and nothing but the new model-level family would notice if one of them stopped agreeing. The SVG codec's 6 drops are in the same position.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Two independent routes, and they are not substitutes. (a) FIELD-LEVEL, already open: extend test_fixtures/expected/codec_field_survival.json -- add fields to the watched list and a mirrored accessor in each port's survival_row. This sees any field without touching the wire format. (b) ORACLE-LEVEL, a design decision that has NOT been taken: teach the canonical test-JSON to emit these keys CONDITIONALLY on non-default, the way it already emits `id` and `fill_rule`. That is additive (no existing golden moves, a grep of the 39 pre-existing .json files in test_fixtures/expected for mode / mask / fill_gradient / stroke_gradient / tool_origin / dash_align_anchors / width_points / stroke_brush returns ZERO hits) but it widens the CROSS_LANGUAGE_TESTING.md contract and must land in both ports in one step. Route (b) is what would let a saturated FIXTURE, rather than a saturated constructor, drive the gate. Repairing the binary codec itself is a third, separate question: it needs a ruling on where new slots go (the format has grown trailing slots twice -- doc index 3 for `symbols`, TAG_LIVE slot 9 for the instance transform -- but a shared common-block extension would have to be appended per element tag, since `unpack_common` reads fixed indices 1..6 of the variant's own array and every variant's payload starts at 7).

coverage_gaps.title: RESOLVED at the per-element transform: the paste offset now reaches a live compound in BOTH ports and is gated by the paste_translate family. What remains OPEN is the paste FLOW around it -- Rust appends to the selected layer, Swift merges by layer name -- which no fixture reaches because op_apply still has no paste verb
coverage_gaps.evidence: THE DIVERGENCE, now DRIVEN rather than read. Adjudicated at tier 1, not by consistency: workspace/actions.yaml §paste specifies 'offset 24 points down and to the right from the original position' against paste_in_place's explicit 'no offset', so this was a written requirement Rust met and Swift did not -- the Python reference has no paste at all (grep: zero hits for 'paste' in workspace_interpreter/). Rust made authoritative on that basis. MEASURED on the new `paste_translate` family before the fix: 2 of 3 vectors failed rust-vs-swift and the zero-offset control passed. Swift returned the compound's operands at (0,0) and (5,0) instead of (24,24) and (29,24) -- the pasted compound exactly on top of its source, invisible, which is the one outcome the offset exists to prevent. A SECOND defect in the same helper surfaced in the same red: its `.group` arm rebuilt Group(children:opacity:transform:locked:) field by field and dropped name, id, visibility, blendMode, mask, isolatedBlending and knockoutGroup, so pasting a NAMED group produced an unnamed one (the Swift copy-site omission class, at a paste). THE FIX deletes the duplicate walk rather than repairing it: `EditClipboard.translateElement` now forwards to `Element.translated(dx:dy:)`, which was already the field-preserving mirror of Rust's `translate_element`, compound arm included -- it was correct all along while the paste path did not call it. WHAT WATCHES IT: test_fixtures/algorithms/paste_translate.json (3 vectors, EXACT, registered in cross_language_algorithms.py) plus JasSwift/Tests/Clipboard/PasteTranslateTests.swift (3 batteries). The family drives `EditClipboard.translateElement` and Rust's `translate_element` -- the functions the PASTE PATHS call -- deliberately NOT Swift's `Element.translated`, which would have been a decoy that never went red. Its result is the whole element serialized through the shared document writer, because a coordinate-only comparison would have seen the compound half and missed the group-name half. The golden was produced by the Rust binary and then VERIFIED independently against the spec by the generator (operands moved by exactly 24, identity intact, zero offset moves nothing) before being written. Mutation proof: restoring the old walk reds both halves in swift, naming both the wrong coordinates and the nil name.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The per-element transform is no longer divergent or unwatched. Three things the corpus still cannot see, and the first is a LIVE divergence found while gating this one: (1) the paste FLOW differs between ports -- Rust's clipboard_read_and_paste appends every pasted child to doc.layers[selected], while Swift's pasteClipboard MERGES BY LAYER NAME and only falls back to the selected layer, so pasting a fragment whose layer name matches an existing layer lands in a different layer in the two ports. Read on this commit, not driven; no ruling exists (actions.yaml specifies the offset and the selection, and is silent on layer targeting). (2) Paste still copies ids verbatim in both ports, so a pasted element can duplicate a live identity -- the same blocked-on-a-cardinality-ruling state as the clear-ids row. (3) Rust's paste body still lives inside a spawn_local closure over Rc<RefCell<AppState>> and a Dioxus Signal, so it is unreachable from cargo test --lib; the new family reaches the helper it calls, not the body.
coverage_gaps.unblock: For the flow: a JYH ruling on layer targeting (does a paste follow the clipboard fragment's layer name, or always land in the active layer?), then the machinery the previous version of this row described -- lift Rust's paste body into a pure function over (Document, Vec<Element>, offset) -> Document, give both ports a `paste` verb in op_apply routed through it, and add one operations vector. The verb is the piece that unblocks (2) as well, since the operations lane already installs the deterministic mint override.

coverage_gaps.evidence: JsonObj::str_val in jas_dioxus/src/geometry/test_json.rs and JsonObj.str in JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/TestJson.swift each apply exactly two replacements (\\ and \") and no U+0000-U+001F escaping. Consistent with that, zero of the 39 test_fixtures/expected/*.json contain an escaped control character.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The byte oracle behind all three codec gates structurally cannot express multi-line text, so no fixture can be added for it until the writers are fixed. It fails LOUDLY (both parsers reject), so it is a ceiling rather than a silent divergence.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Add U+0000-U+001F escaping to both writers, then add a text fixture containing a newline.

coverage_gaps.title: Every fixture that reaches a DUPLICATION verb -- artboard duplicate, Layers-panel duplicate, clipboard paste -- copies an id-less element, so a copy wearing its source's identity is invisible to the whole corpus
coverage_gaps.evidence: Measured on this commit. (a) The one cross-language vector that reaches a duplication verb is operations/artboard_duplicate (driven by cross_language_test.rs operation_artboard_duplicate); its setup SVG carries no id= attribute on any element, so it ran GREEN before and after the id defect was repaired. (b) The two landed unit batteries for doc.clone_at (renderer.rs doc_clone_at_then_insert_after_duplicates and production_route_duplicate_layer_selection_journals_one_insert_after) build their layers through make_state_with_layers, which hard-codes id: None -- likewise green in both directions. (c) The two landed batteries for artboard_duplicate_init build their rects with CommonProps::default(). Driven consequence, this wave: artboard_duplicate_init pushed Rc::new((**child).clone()) and doc.clone_at returned get_element(..).cloned(), both id included, so an id walk after duplicating a group yielded ["g-outer","r-inner","g-outer","r-inner"]. Both are repaired in Rust WITHOUT ONE GOLDEN BYTE MOVING. Same shape as identity-law-boolean-operands-id-less, one lane over.
coverage_gaps.blocks: The duplication verbs could be fixed, unfixed or inverted between the two ports and no cross-language golden would notice. Two live consequences the corpus still cannot see: (1) JasSwift has not been checked against the repaired Rust rule at these verbs, so the ports may now DISAGREE on whether a duplicate is born id-less; (2) workspace::clipboard::clipboard_read_and_paste remains UNREPAIRED in Rust -- it pastes translate_element(elem, dx, dy), which is ..e.clone() with the id, from the internal clipboard; and the SVG paste path runs dedupe_element_ids over the PASTED fragment alone, which is blind to ids already live in the target document. That site is unreachable from cargo test --lib (it lives inside a spawn_local closure over Rc<RefCell<AppState>> and a Dioxus Signal), so it has neither a unit battery nor a corpus vector.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Fixture work plus one refactor. Fixtures: give the artboard-duplicate setup SVG ids, names and a nested identified child, and add a duplicate_layer_selection vector to the ACTION lane (which already installs the deterministic mint override via recorder::replay::run_action_case); assert id ABSENCE on the copy and id SURVIVAL on the source rather than literal ids. Refactor, before paste can be pinned at all: lift the paste body out of clipboard_read_and_paste into a pure function over (Document, Vec<Element>, offset) -> Document so a red can be shown at the layer that owns the bug.

coverage_gaps.title: Rust's CompoundShape carries common.name and Swift's CompoundShape has NO name field at all, so a named compound cannot round-trip through the Swift port -- a model-level divergence against the any-element-carries-a-name rule
coverage_gaps.evidence: MEASURED on this commit while building the paste_translate family, then isolated out of it. Feeding both roundtrip binaries a compound_shape test-json element carrying "name": "hull", Rust returned "name":"hull" and Swift returned "name":null. Two causes, one above the other: (a) JasSwift/Sources/Geometry/LiveElement.swift's `CompoundShape` declares no `name` property, and its own doc comment says so -- "No name field is intended for live elements" -- while jas_dioxus's `CompoundShape` holds a full `CommonProps` including `name`; the same asymmetry applies to Swift's `.reference`, `.recorded` and `.generated` payloads. (b) Consistent with (a), TestJson.swift's `parseElement` "live" arm forwards `id` and not `name`, so the key is dropped on the way in even where a slot existed. The house rule is that ANY element carries a name (SVG inkscape:label), and Rust's own `rich_compound` fixture asserts `name: Some("hull")`.
coverage_gaps.blocks: Any fixture that names a live element is VACUOUS in Swift -- the field arrives nil and the golden either records nil or the swift lane reds for a reason unrelated to the vector's subject, which is exactly what happened to the first draft of paste_translate (its compound is deliberately unnamed, with a comment saying why). More broadly, the Layers panel cannot show a user-given name for a compound shape in JasSwift, and the preservation law's name-carry clauses cannot be expressed over live elements there at all.
coverage_gaps.unblock: Not a fixture problem and not smuggled into this wave: adding `name` to Swift's four live conformers is precisely the copy-site omission class in reverse -- every construction site of every conformer must be enumerated, and the house's own answer to that class is to make the new initializer parameter REQUIRED so the compiler lists the sites. Do it as its own wave, Swift-only, with the Rust side already correct; then name the compound in paste_translate and in the clear-ids probe vector.

coverage_gaps.title: Rust's paste appends to the SELECTED layer; Swift's paste MERGES BY LAYER NAME and only then falls back to the selected layer -- read, not driven, and no fixture can reach either flow
coverage_gaps.evidence: READ on this commit while fixing the paste OFFSET, and stated at exactly that strength. jas_dioxus/src/workspace/clipboard.rs `clipboard_read_and_paste`: for every pasted layer's children it pushes into `doc.layers[idx]` where `idx = doc.selected_layer`, with no name lookup anywhere in the function. JasSwift/Sources/Clipboard/EditClipboard.swift `pasteClipboard`: for every pasted layer it searches `newLayers` for one whose `name` equals the pasted layer's name and uses that index, `?? doc.selectedLayer`. So pasting an SVG fragment whose layer is named "Layer 1" into a document that already has a "Layer 1" lands in that layer in Swift and in whatever layer is selected in Rust.
coverage_gaps.blocks: A prime-directive divergence in the paste FLOW, one level up from the per-element offset that the paste_translate family now gates. It is invisible to every gate for the same reason the offset was: op_apply has no paste verb in either port, so neither the operations corpus nor the preservation gate can express a paste, and the gesture corpus declares no clipboard tool.
coverage_gaps.unblock: A ruling FIRST, because both behaviours are defensible and workspace/actions.yaml §paste is silent -- it specifies the 24pt offset and that the pasted objects become the selection, and says nothing about layer targeting. Choosing one here would be inventing a ruling. Once ruled, the machinery is the same paste verb the row above needs.
